Kei: Heads-up: Support called about a customer seeing many small token charges yesterday evening. Traces point to a burst of WS reconnects that each appear to bill ~10-30 tokens.
Nina: Any pattern in client or SDK?
Kei: Two interesting signals: 1) all affected clients use `rdw-sdk-js` v1.4.x, 2) reconnects show identical resume_id but different `seq` numbers. Example: ```text
trace=tx99 resume=R-77 seq=102 billed=12 upstream=a
trace=tx99 resume=R-77 seq=103 billed=15 upstream=b
```
Omar: That suggests resume succeeded and continued on new shard (seq advanced) but meter considered them separate sessions because we dedupe on resume_id only and we tag by route.
Priya: Console aggregated by route so it looked like two sessions. Also noticed telemetry sampling was higher for reconnect events, which skewed UI percentages.
Kei: Also saw two SDK variants: older SDK retries immediately after networkidle, newer SDK waits for PONG timeout before reconnect. Mixed fleet yields overlaps and both shards accept resume.
Nina: Could we use the `seq` field to detect continued stream vs duplicate resume? If seq increases monotonically we should NOT count it as a new billing resume.
Omar: Good idea. Proposal: meter dedupe key = hash(account + resume_id + floor(seq/10)) so small seq advances within same 10-event bucket are considered same session. TTL 20s. That avoids counting a continuing stream as duplicate while still deduping rapid duplicate resumes with same seq.
Priya: Edge-case: some legitimate reconnects will resume at same seq if client replayed. floor(seq/10) might hide true duplicates. Maybe use last_seen_seq per-resume and only dedupe if new seq <= last_seen_seq + 1?
Kei: Simpler: store last_seen_seq (int) in meter memstore, if incoming seq <= last_seen_seq then treat as duplicate and drop billing; if seq > last_seen_seq then accept and update. That seems intuitive. TTL 30s.
Omar: Implementation note: per-metric-shard memstore for speed, fallback to redis for cross-worker check on miss. Feature flag `meter_resume_seq_guard`. Low-latency path must remain fast.
Priya: UX/Console: add a tooltip on per-route billing that explains "small reconnect charges may be de-duplicated by seq guard" and show a short rollout banner when feature is active. Also add a panel: `duplicate_resume_by_seq_rate` by account.
telemetry-bot: Suggested PromQL: `sum by (account)(rate(resume_reconnects_total[5m]) - rate(resume_seq_advance_total[5m]))` -> indicates reconnects not accompanied by seq advance.
billing-bot: If duplicate billing is confirmed, we should auto-credit obvious windows. How do we detect those?
Nina: Use a heuristic: for an account, find short windows (<=60s) where billed_tokens spikes and >80% of reconnects for that window are marked duplicate by seq-guard (post-hoc). Flag for manual review and auto-credit if >1000 tokens.
Kei: Rollout plan: 1) Implement meter_resume_seq_guard behind flag, memstore-only, canary 5% global with apac focus. 2) Add console panel + banner. 3) After 6h evaluation, flip redis cross-worker dedupe and increase canary. 4) Add SDK guidance: prefer waiting for PONG and backoff.
Omar: Also add a telemetry tag indicating SDK variant (rdw-sdk-js=1.4 vs 1.5) so we can track adoption. Nina, can Console expose that per-account?
Nina: Yes, add `client_sdk_version` tag in traces and a small Console table.
Priya: Action items: Omar -> PR for seq_guard + memstore + flag. Nina -> dashboard panel + banner + trace tag. Kei -> ops note + billing heuristic. Omar -> start 5% canary and post metric links.
Kei: One more: put an alert in #oncall: if `duplicate_resume_by_seq_rate` > 0.5% and `billed_tokens` delta > 2000 in 10m, page SRE.
telemetry-bot: Alert rule created: `resume-seq-duplicate-high` (thresholds configured).
Kei: Thanks all. Let's keep this thread updated with canary numbers. If we see regressions, we can roll back the flag quickly. :thumbsup:
Priya: I'll coordinate credits after we have the post-canary dedupe counts.
Omar: Starting canary now (meter-seq-guard v0.1) -> 5% traffic global. Posting dashboards in 10m.
